# nostr-veil

> Nostr has a standard for publishing trust scores (NIP-85), but ordinary
> assertions name the provider and multi-party reputation can expose a visible
> contributor graph -- making sensitive contexts like whistleblowing, abuse
> reporting, or political dissent hard to support safely.
> nostr-veil adds ring-signature privacy so scores are verifiable without
> exposing contributors.

nostr-veil is a TypeScript library for anonymous trust assertions on Nostr. It
wraps standard NIP-85 trust score events in ring signatures -- a cryptographic
technique where a verifier can confirm "someone in this group signed" without
knowing who. The output is a standard NIP-85 event that any Nostr app reads
unchanged -- privacy-aware apps can additionally verify the cryptographic
proofs via additive `veil-*` tags.

## ForgeSworn ecosystem

- [ForgeSworn library guide](https://forgesworn.dev/llms.txt): Find related libraries, tools and integration guides by task and runtime.
- [ForgeSworn on GitHub](https://github.com/forgesworn): Browse the organisation’s public repositories.
- [Project source](https://github.com/forgesworn/nostr-veil): Canonical source repository, documentation and release information.

## Getting Started

```bash
npm install nostr-veil
```

```ts
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js'
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js'
import {
  createTrustCircle, contributeAssertion, aggregateContributions, verifyProof, signEvent, NIP85_KINDS,
} from 'nostr-veil'

// 0. Generate keys. nostr-veil takes 64-char lowercase hex strings everywhere.
function generateKeypair() {
  const secret = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey()            // Uint8Array (noble v2)
  return { privkey: bytesToHex(secret), pubkey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secret)) }
}
const alice = generateKeypair()
const bob = generateKeypair()
const carol = generateKeypair()
const subject = generateKeypair()      // the account being scored; only its pubkey is used
const aggregator = generateKeypair()   // publishes the result; does not need to be a circle member
const subjectPubkey = subject.pubkey

// 1. Define a circle of three anonymous members
const circle = createTrustCircle([alice.pubkey, bob.pubkey, carol.pubkey])

// 2. Each member contributes independently -- identity hidden inside the ring.
//    memberIndex is the position in the SORTED circle.members, so use indexOf.
const aliceContribution = contributeAssertion(
  circle, subjectPubkey, { followers: 820, rank: 74 }, alice.privkey, circle.members.indexOf(alice.pubkey),
)
const bobContribution = contributeAssertion(
  circle, subjectPubkey, { followers: 900, rank: 80 }, bob.privkey, circle.members.indexOf(bob.pubkey),
)

// 3. Aggregate into a standard NIP-85 kind 30382 event (an unsigned EventTemplate)
const assertion = aggregateContributions(circle, subjectPubkey, [aliceContribution, bobContribution])

// 4. The aggregator signs it as an ordinary Nostr event and publishes it
const signed = signEvent(assertion, aggregator.privkey)

// 5. Verify: two distinct signers agreed, no names attached
const result = verifyProof(signed, { expectedKind: NIP85_KINDS.USER, requireAggregate: 'median' })
// { valid: true, circleSize: 3, threshold: 2, distinctSigners: 2,
//   subjectInRing: false, independentSigners: 2, errors: [] }
```

Formats: pubkeys are 64-char lowercase hex x-only strings; every `privateKey`
argument (`contributeAssertion`, `signEvent`, `createSignedDeploymentBundle`) is a
64-char hex string. A `Uint8Array` is rejected, so convert noble byte keys with
`bytesToHex`. `circle.members.indexOf(pubkey)` is the only safe `memberIndex`: a
wrong index throws `Private key does not match ring member at signerIndex` in the
helpers that take a private key. The `*Async` helpers hand the index to the
signer and cannot check it, as a ring signature hides who signed.
The aggregator is whoever collects the contributions and publishes the event;
the ring proofs are in the `veil-sig` tags and `verifyProof` does not check the
outer Nostr signature, so call `verifySignedEvent(event)` on events fetched from
untrusted relays. Pass `expectedKind` because v1 proofs are not kind-bound.

## Key Concepts

- **Trust circle**: A fixed group of public keys that can contribute scores anonymously. Created with `createTrustCircle()`. Minimum 2 members, maximum 1000.
- **Contribution**: A single member's anonymous vote, wrapped in a ring signature. A duplicate-detection token (key image) prevents double-voting without revealing the voter.
- **Aggregation**: Contributions are combined (median by default) into a standard NIP-85 event with `veil-ring`, `veil-threshold`, `veil-agg`, and `veil-sig` tags. Use `aggregateContributions` for kind 30382 user assertions, `aggregateEventContributions` for kind 30383 event assertions, `aggregateAddressableContributions` for kind 30384 addressable assertions, and `aggregateIdentifierContributions` for kind 30385 identifier assertions. The typed contribution helpers sign proof v2 by default, binding kind and subject hint tags; aggregators follow the contributions' version.
- **Verification**: `verifyProof()` confirms each ring signature is valid, duplicate-detection tokens are distinct, election IDs match, and the threshold is met -- all without learning who signed. Pass `{ requireProofVersion: 'v2' }` when a workflow must reject legacy v1 proofs. Pass `{ requireAggregate: 'median' }` (or whichever function you expect) too: the publisher chooses the `veil-agg` tag and the circle does not sign it, so the same signatures republished as a `max` or a `min` verify as well. Under `sum`, `mean`, `min` or `max` also pass `contributionBounds`, because a key image stops a second contribution, not one large value.
- **Federation scope**: Circles sharing a `scope` (set via `createTrustCircle(members, { scope })`) produce matching key images for members they have in common, so `verifyFederation()` can verify several scoped events about one subject and count distinct contributors across circles without double-counting anyone in more than one. The events must share kind, subject, scope and electionId (same proof version and, for v2, the same bound subject tag and value); it takes the same options as `verifyProof`.
- **Election ID**: v1 format `veil:v1:<scope-or-circleId>:<subject>`. v2 adds assertion kind and subject hint tag/value to prevent cross-kind replay; the typed contribute helpers sign v2 by default, `contributeAssertion` v1, and aggregators follow the contributions' version.
- **Signing**: `signEvent(template, privateKey)` is exported from the root package (not from a subpath). `privateKey` is a 64-char hex string. It computes the event ID, signs with Schnorr, and returns a complete `SignedEvent`. `verifySignedEvent(event)` and `computeEventId(event)` are root-only too.
- **Aggregation options**: `{ aggregate: 'median' | 'mean' | 'sum' | 'min' | 'max' }` (default median) is recorded in the `veil-agg` tag and `verifyProof` reads it from there, so a summed tally verifies with a bare `verifyProof(event)`. A custom `{ aggregateFn }` (or bare function) is recorded as `veil-agg: custom` and must also be passed to `verifyProof` (`{ aggregateFn }`), otherwise it fails with `veil-agg is "custom": pass the aggregate function via options to verify the metric tags`. `median` and `mean` round to integers; `sum`, `min` and `max` do not. `{ contributionBounds: { rank: { min: 0, max: 1, integer: true, required: true } } }` makes aggregation throw on a contribution outside the bounds (`required` also refuses a contribution that leaves the metric out, which would otherwise still count as a signer), and `contributionBoundViolations(metrics, bounds)` finds such a contribution first.

## API Surface

Three subpath exports (`nostr-veil/nip85`, `nostr-veil/proof`, `nostr-veil/profiles`), plus a root (`nostr-veil`) that re-exports all three and adds the signing helpers `signEvent`, `verifySignedEvent` and `computeEventId`, which exist only at the root:

**`nostr-veil/nip85`** -- NIP-85 foundation (kinds 30382-30385 + 10040):
`buildUserAssertion(pubkey, metrics)`, `buildEventAssertion(eventId, metrics)`, `buildAddressableAssertion(address, metrics)`, `buildIdentifierAssertion(identifier, kTag, metrics)`, `buildProviderDeclaration(providers, encryptedContent?)` where providers is `{ kind, metric, servicePubkey, relayHint }[]`, `parseAssertion(event)`, `parseProviderDeclaration(event, decryptFn?)`, `validateAssertion(event, options?)`, `validateAssertionStrict(event)`, `validateProviderDeclarationStrict(event)`, `assertionFilter({ kind, subject?, provider? })`, `providerFilter(pubkey)`, `NIP85_KINDS`

**`nostr-veil/proof`** -- Ring-signature proof layer:
`createTrustCircle`, `contributeAssertion`, `contributeEventAssertion`, `contributeAddressableAssertion`, `contributeIdentifierAssertion`, `contributeAssertionAsync`, `contributeEventAssertionAsync`, `contributeAddressableAssertionAsync`, `contributeIdentifierAssertionAsync` (the same four with an external `LsagSigner` in place of the private key: `signer.lsagSign({ message, ring, signerIndex, electionId })` returns the LSAG signature, which is verified and stripped to its signature fields before use), `contributionBoundViolations`, `aggregateContributions`, `aggregateEventContributions`, `aggregateAddressableContributions`, `aggregateIdentifierContributions`, `verifyProof`, `verifyFederation`, `canonicalMessage`, `canonicalMessageV2`, `computeCircleId`

**`nostr-veil/profiles`** -- Safer deployment profiles:
`USE_CASE_PROFILES`, `USE_CASE_PROFILE_BY_ID`, `verifyUseCaseProfile`,
`createCircleManifest`, `verifyCircleManifest`, `createDeploymentPolicy`,
`verifyDeploymentPolicy`, `createSignedDeploymentBundle`,
`verifySignedDeploymentBundle`, `verifyDeploymentBundle`, `verifyProductionDeployment`,
`createProductionDecisionReport`, `verifyProductionDeploymentReport`,
`createAdmissionChallenge`, `createAdmissionPresentation`,
`verifyAdmissionPresentation`, `verifyAdmissionRequest`,
`validateUseCaseProfileDefinition`, `VerificationIssue`,
`VerificationIssueCode`, `explainVerificationIssue`,
`remediationForIssue`, and canonical subject helpers. Run
`validateUseCaseProfileDefinition(profile)` for custom profiles to catch
NIP-85 route mismatches, unsupported metrics, missing safety metadata, and
overclaiming warnings before production use. Use
`verifyProductionDeployment` with pinned trusted publisher pubkeys for
production relay-fetched assertions; it also requires expiring bundles and
signed events by default. A proof does not say who published it or when: the
ring signatures are public and carry no time, so anyone can republish a subset
of them, or an old proof under a new `created_at`, with their own key. Where
the circle has a designated publisher, name its key in the policy
(`acceptedPublishers`). Use decision reports and issue explanations to turn
failures into concrete operator actions instead of only showing negative
results. Built-in profiles expose `proofClaims`, `proofLimitations`,
`requiredControls`, and `recommendedActions`; use those fields when explaining
what nostr-veil proves and what the application must still verify.
Deployment policies can also require `companionEvidence` for external facts the
proof cannot prove, such as `npm-provenance`, `sbom`,
`vulnerability-feed`, `nip05-resolution`, `https-probe`, `dns-owner-check`,
`list-revision-fetch`, `sample-review`, and `correction-channel`. Missing,
failed, stale, or wrong-subject companion evidence fails closed.
Canonical subject helpers cover Nostr-native subjects plus relays, service
endpoints, NIP-05, domains, LNURLp, NIP-96, npm packages, package artefact
digests, git repositories, GitHub repositories, maintainers, vendors, sources,
and method-scoped credential verifiers. Prefer those helpers before signing so
every contributor scores the same verifier-compatible identifier.

## Options and Types

- Metrics: `Record<string, number>`, finite (NaN and Infinity throw), integers not required, published as `String(value)`. Metric names must not be a single character, start with `veil-`, be a Nostr tag with its own meaning (`expiration`, `alt`, `client`, `nonce`, `content-warning`), or be `__proto__`: contributing throws `Metric name "<name>" is reserved: ...`, aggregation rejects such a contribution, and `verifyProof` rejects an event whose signed metrics use one. This stops a single circle member from injecting a tag such as `expiration` into the published event. The publisher can still set a NIP-40 expiration or a NIP-31 alt on the event it signs: pass `{ expiration, alt }` to the aggregator. The circle does not sign these two tags; the publisher's own Nostr signature covers them, as it covers `content`. `verifyProof` accepts at most 128 metrics of up to 64 characters by default. The `nostr-veil/nip85` builders use typed optional metrics: `UserMetrics` (30382: `followers`, `rank`, `first_created_at`, `post_cnt`, `reply_cnt`, `reactions_cnt`, `zap_amt_recd`, `zap_amt_sent`, `zap_cnt_recd`, `zap_cnt_sent`, `zap_avg_amt_day_recd`, `zap_avg_amt_day_sent`, `reports_cnt_recd`, `reports_cnt_sent`, `t`, `active_hours_start`, `active_hours_end`), `EventMetrics` (30383/30384: `rank`, `comment_cnt`, `quote_cnt`, `repost_cnt`, `reaction_cnt`, `zap_cnt`, `zap_amount`), `IdentifierMetrics` (30385: `rank`, `comment_cnt`, `reaction_cnt`).
- Aggregation options for `aggregateContributions` and the typed `aggregate*Contributions` helpers: a bare `(values: number[]) => number`, or `{ aggregate?: 'median' | 'mean' | 'sum' | 'min' | 'max', aggregateFn?, proofVersion?: 'v1' | 'v2', kind?, expiration?: number, alt?: string, contributionBounds?: Record<string, { min?, max?, integer?, required? }> }` (`contributionBounds` throws on a contribution outside the bounds; `kind` is legacy and only on `aggregateContributions`; `expiration` (unix seconds) and `alt` emit publisher tags that the circle does not sign and `verifyProof` does not read as metrics: at most one of each, `alt` non-empty; `verifyProof` does not check expiry against the clock, but the profile verifiers reject an assertion whose `expiration` is at or before `now`; trust these tags only after checking the outer Nostr signature; `aggregate` wins over `aggregateFn`; an unknown name throws `Unknown aggregate function: <name>`).
- `verifyProof(event, options?)`: a bare aggregate function, or `{ aggregateFn?, expectedKind?: number, requireProofVersion?: 'v1' | 'v2', requireAggregate?: 'median' | 'mean' | 'sum' | 'min' | 'max' | 'custom', contributionBounds?: Record<string, { min?, max?, integer?, required? }>, rejectSubjectInRing?: boolean, limits?: Partial<VerifyLimits> }`. `requireAggregate` rejects an event whose `veil-agg` tag names another function (`veil-agg is "max" but "median" is required`; no tag reads as `median`); `contributionBounds` rejects an event holding a contribution outside the bounds, and malformed bounds fail the proof. `DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMITS` is `maxRingSize` 1000, `maxSigPayloadBytes` 128000, `maxSignedMessageBytes` 16384, `maxMetricCount` 128, `maxMetricNameLength` 64, `maxSubjectLength` 512 (UTF-16 code units of the `d` tag: no longer subject can be signed, as the LSAG election id holds it and is limited to 512 bytes), and `maxTagCount`, which, left out, is `maxRingSize + maxMetricCount + 72` (1,200), so it rises with the ring limit. A proof's signatures, distinct metric names and fixed tags must together be within it, so a proof whose members sign different metric names can need it raised. An event with more tags, a tag name longer than `maxMetricNameLength` (or 14, the longest proof tag name) that does not begin `veil-`, or a longer `d` tag fails before any tag is read. Each limit must be a non-negative number, `Infinity` to lift it, and any other value, such as `NaN` or a string, fails the proof. Returns `{ valid, circleSize, threshold, distinctSigners, subjectInRing, independentSigners, errors }`; when the subject is a ring member one signature may be theirs, so compare `independentSigners` with your threshold or pass `rejectSubjectInRing: true`. A metric, `d` or `k` tag with anything after its value is invalid (the circle signs only name and value), and a `k` tag is accepted only on kind 30385. A second `veil-ring`, `veil-threshold`, `veil-agg`, `veil-version` or `veil-scope` tag, or extra elements on any of them or on `veil-sig`, is invalid; unknown `veil-*` tags are ignored, though they count towards the tag limit.
- `contributeAssertion(..., options?)`: `{ proofVersion?, kind?, subjectTag?: 'p' | 'e' | 'a' | 'k', subjectTagValue? }`; the typed helpers take only `{ proofVersion? }` and sign v2 unless given `'v1'`; `contributeAssertion` defaults to v1. `canonicalMessageV2(circleId, subject, metrics, context)` needs `context` as `{ kind, subjectTag, subjectTagValue }`, all required (non-negative safe integer kind, `p`/`e`/`a`/`k` tag, non-empty value).
- `parseAssertion(event)` returns `{ kind: number, subject: string, metrics: Record<string, string | number> }` (subject is the `d` tag value, metric values are raw tag strings; `expiration` and `alt` are left out with the other non-metric tags, so, on an event that passes `verifyProof`, `metrics` holds only circle-signed values). `parseProviderDeclaration(event)` returns `ParsedProvider[]` of `{ kind, metric, servicePubkey, relayHint }`, or a Promise of it when given `decryptFn: (ciphertext: string) => Promise<string>`.
- Profiles options (timestamps are Unix seconds; `now` defaults to the current time, and a `now` that cannot be compared, such as `NaN`, fails every verifier that takes one, with `verification.now_invalid` in every result that carries issue codes, which an admission request's result does only in its `deployment`, and circle manifest and admission presentation results do not; a `maxAgeSeconds` that is not a non-negative integer fails with `policy.max_age_seconds_invalid`, a `minDistinctSigners` that is not a positive integer with `policy.min_distinct_signers_invalid`, and a `metricPolicies` `min` or `max` that is not a finite number with `policy.metric_policy_invalid`). `verifyUseCaseProfile` and `verifyDeploymentPolicy`, and the bundle, production and admission verifiers through them, take `limits` as `verifyProof` does: an event over one is rejected as `event.limit_exceeded` before any check reads its tags, none of its metrics is read, and the report fails its circle, profile, proof and metric controls; a limit that is not a non-negative number fails the run as `verification.limits_invalid`, and no event is checked beyond its Nostr signature. `createCircleManifest`: required `issuedAt`, `members`, `name`, `profileIds`, `purpose`; optional `expiresAt`, `status`, `supersedes`, `revokedCircleIds`, `contact`, `evidenceProcess`, `policyUri`. `createDeploymentPolicy(profile, options)`: required `expectedSubject` plus at least one active circle via `acceptedCircleIds` or `circleManifests`; optional `expectedSubjectTagValue`, `id`, `maxAgeSeconds`, `maxFutureSeconds` (default 60: how far ahead of the verifier's clock `created_at` may be before the assertion fails with `assertion.created_at_future`; 0 allows no skew, and setting it with `maxAgeSeconds` 0 is an error), `minDistinctSigners`, `metricPolicies` (`{ [metric]: { required?, min?, max?, integer? } }`, bounds on the published aggregate), `aggregate` (default: the profile's; every built-in profile pins `median`, or `sum` for `anonymous-group-decisions`), `contributionBounds` (`{ [metric]: { min?, max?, integer?, required? } }`, bounds on each contribution), `rejectUnknownMetrics` (default false), `requireNostrSignature` (default false), `acceptedPublishers` (hex pubkeys that may sign the assertion events; naming any turns `requireNostrSignature` on, and an event from any other key fails with `event.publisher_unaccepted`), `companionEvidence`, `allowSupersededCircleIds`, `now`. `createSignedDeploymentBundle(policy, options)`: required `id`, `issuedAt`, `privateKey`; optional `expiresAt`. `verifySignedDeploymentBundle(bundle, { now?, trustedPublishers? })`. `verifyDeploymentBundle(events, bundle, options?)` takes `aggregateFn`, `companionEvidence`, `limits`, `now`, `trustedPublishers`. `verifyProductionDeployment` adds `requireBundleExpiry` and `requireSignedEvents`, both true by default, and returns `{ decision: 'accept' | 'reject', valid, errors, issues, bundle, deployment }`. Without a valid `trustedPublishers` entry, bundle verification fails with `no trusted bundle publishers configured`. The bundled policy is applied only when the bundle is authentic (valid signature from a `trustedPublishers` key): for any other bundle `deployment` is a rejection with no findings, the report's policy controls read `not-checked`, and its `profile`, `policyId` and `subject` are blank. A malformed event, or a malformed bundle that is not authentic, is rejected with an issue code, and a malformed admission presentation is denied with an error; no verifier throws on any of them. In the policy of an authentic bundle, each field the verifier reads must be absent or of its type, and `null` is not absent: one that is not is rejected as `policy.field_invalid`, `profile.field_invalid` or `circle.manifest_field_invalid`, nothing else in that policy is checked, and the report's policy controls read `not-checked`, though a value with a check of its own, such as a time window, the signer threshold, a metric bound or the accepted publishers, keeps its own code and the run goes on. A bundle that stored a `null` `expectedSubjectTagValue`, or a `null` `required` or `integer` in a metric entry, as `createDeploymentPolicy` could, must be reissued. The verifier's own options are not covered.
- Issue codes: read them from `issues` on a verification result (`issues[i]` is the issue for `errors[i]`). Each code is given where its error is raised, so text inside an event cannot change it. Do not derive a code from an `errors` string: the messages quote tag names and kinds from the event.

## Profiles Example

Continuing from the quick start. The built-in `USER_REPUTATION_ABUSE_REPORTING_PROFILE` needs proof v2, at least three distinct signers and an assertion no older than 300 seconds.

```ts
import {
  USER_REPUTATION_ABUSE_REPORTING_PROFILE,
  createDeploymentPolicy,
  createSignedDeploymentBundle,
  verifyProductionDeployment,
} from 'nostr-veil/profiles'

const operator = generateKeypair() // deployment operator, separate from circle members
const contributions = [alice, bob, carol].map(member => contributeAssertion(
  circle, subjectPubkey, { rank: 80 }, member.privkey, circle.members.indexOf(member.pubkey), { proofVersion: 'v2' },
))
const event = signEvent(
  aggregateContributions(circle, subjectPubkey, contributions, { proofVersion: 'v2' }),
  aggregator.privkey,
)

const policy = createDeploymentPolicy(USER_REPUTATION_ABUSE_REPORTING_PROFILE, {
  acceptedCircleIds: [circle.circleId],
  expectedSubject: subjectPubkey,
  acceptedPublishers: [aggregator.pubkey], // nobody else may republish the circle's signatures
  requireNostrSignature: true,       // verifyProductionDeployment needs this; naming acceptedPublishers also turns it on
})
const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)
const bundle = createSignedDeploymentBundle(policy, {
  id: 'abuse-reporting-2026-01',
  issuedAt: now,
  expiresAt: now + 24 * 60 * 60,     // verifyProductionDeployment rejects a bundle without expiry
  privateKey: operator.privkey,
})

const verdict = verifyProductionDeployment([event], bundle, { trustedPublishers: [operator.pubkey] })
// verdict.decision === 'accept'; a bundle signed by another key fails with `bundle.signer_untrusted`,
// and an event signed by any key but the aggregator's with `event.publisher_unaccepted`
```

See [examples/production-recipes.ts](https://github.com/forgesworn/nostr-veil/blob/main/examples/production-recipes.ts) for six production-shaped gates with companion evidence.

## CLI

The package installs a `nostr-veil` binary:

```bash
nostr-veil assert user <pubkey> [--json '<metrics>']
nostr-veil assert event <event-id> [--json '<metrics>']
nostr-veil assert address <address> [--json '<metrics>']
nostr-veil assert identifier <id> <k-tag> [--json '<metrics>']
nostr-veil provider-declare [--json '<entries>']
nostr-veil verify '<event-json>' [--kind <n>] [--aggregate <fn>]
nostr-veil --help
```

`assert` and `provider-declare` build plain NIP-85 events (kinds 30382 to 30385 and 10040), not ring-signed ones, sign them with the key in `NOSTR_SECRET_KEY` (64-char hex) or the file named by `NOSTR_SECRET_KEY_FILE` (takes precedence), and print the signed event as JSON on stdout. `--json` takes a JSON object of metrics (`provider-declare`: an array of `{ kind, metric, servicePubkey, relayHint }`). `verify` needs no key: `<event-json>` is an inline JSON string, not a file path (`nostr-veil verify "$(cat event.json)" --kind 30382`). Options may come before or after it, as `--kind 30382` or `--kind=30382`, and an unknown or repeated option is an error, never dropped in silence. `--kind` takes a non-negative integer and applies `expectedKind`. `--aggregate` takes `median`, `mean`, `sum`, `min` or `max` and applies `requireAggregate`; without it `verify` accepts whichever function the event names. It prints the `verifyProof` result as JSON and exits 0 even when `valid` is false, so read `valid` rather than the exit code.

## Limits

nostr-veil hides which public ring member contributed. It does not hide the ring
membership list, individual anonymous metric values, network/timing metadata, or
whether the circle was socially well-chosen. Shared federation scopes intentionally
reveal cross-circle overlap by key image while still hiding the contributor's identity.
Use operational controls for the boundary: circle admission and rotation, evidence
workflow, appeals, identifier canonicalisation, expiry, revocation, batching,
transport privacy, and service-specific checks.

## Use-Case Mapping

Use `aggregateContributions` for user reputation, abuse reporting, source
corroboration, onboarding vouches, AI agent vouches from a human-curated
circle, and pubkey-backed trade reputation. Use
`aggregateEventContributions` for event and claim verification. Use
`aggregateAddressableContributions` for long-form review, research, proposals,
lists, and labeler profiles. Use `aggregateIdentifierContributions` for relays,
services, packages, releases, maintainers, NIP-05 identifiers, domains, vendors,
credential verifiers, and other external identifiers; the kind 30385 `k` tag is
the NIP-73 identifier type (`web`, `isbn`, `podcast:guid` and so on), and the
built-in profiles use decimal `k` namespaces for subjects NIP-73 has no type for.
Verifier and issuer legitimacy profiles answer "who verifies the verifier?" by
scoring a method-scoped subject such as
`verifier:proof-of-person:in-person:<pubkey>` before a community accepts
Attestr-style, NIP-VA-style, or other credential artefacts. For pubkey-bound
relay/community admission, keep the NIP-85 vouch as kind 30382 and use the
admission helpers as a separate challenge/presentation companion. The live
admission-gate example publishes that kind 30382 vouch plus a separate NIP-78
kind 30078 deployment-bundle carrier to a relay, fetches both back, and verifies
the fetched material with `verifyAdmissionRequest()`. Kind 30078 is only a
transport wrapper, not a NIP-85 assertion. For anonymous group decisions, voting,
and petitions, aggregate a `rank` ballot with `{ aggregate: 'sum' }` over
`aggregateEventContributions` for a verifiable one-vote-per-member tally, and
verify it through the profile or with `requireAggregate: 'sum'` and
`contributionBounds: { rank: { min: 0, max: 1, integer: true, required: true } }`,
because a key image stops a second ballot, not a ballot worth more than one,
and `required` rejects a signer who cast no ballot; the
summed `rank` is bounded to 0-100, so it suits small electorates (boards,
committees, panels), while a petition counts distinct signatories with
`distinctSigners`. An event grows with ring size times signers (a ring of 100
with 10 signers is about 80 KiB), so both suit small circles. Credential co-signing, anonymous group voting, and fully
anonymous gated access remain future profiles: nostr-veil can provide the
threshold proof, but those flows need separate credential, ballot-format,
coercion-resistance, session, revocation, and transport rules.

Use-case pages are implementation profiles. Each page should identify the
subject shape, helper, metric meaning, proof version, verifier action, proof
boundary, and the operational controls needed outside nostr-veil. Caveats
should be paired with concrete controls such as evidence workflow,
canonicalisation, expiry, revocation, transport privacy, Sybil policy, or a
companion protocol.
For supported off-chain controls, prefer the companion-evidence requirement and
collector/resolver helpers over hand-written `pass` records:
`packageReleaseCompanionEvidenceRequirements()` with
`collectPackageReleaseCompanionEvidence()` or
`resolvePackageReleaseCompanionEvidence()`,
`nip05DomainCompanionEvidenceRequirements()` with
`collectNip05DomainCompanionEvidence()` or
`resolveNip05DomainCompanionEvidence()`, and
`listLabelerCompanionEvidenceRequirements()` with
`collectListLabelerCompanionEvidence()` or
`resolveListLabelerCompanionEvidence()`.
Run `npm run test:companion-evidence` for the deterministic collector smoke
test. Run `npm run test:companion-evidence:live` when you intentionally want
live npm, OSV, NIP-05, HTTPS, and relay I/O; package checks may fail closed
unless npm exposes trusted-publishing provenance and SBOM observations are
available.

## Companion Libraries

These are not dependencies but complement nostr-veil:

- [nsec-tree](https://github.com/forgesworn/nsec-tree) -- Generate separate anonymous identities from a single master key
- [canary-kit](https://github.com/forgesworn/canary-kit) -- Detect when someone is being coerced (duress signals)
- [signet](https://github.com/forgesworn/signet) -- Decentralised identity verification for Nostr
- [dominion](https://github.com/forgesworn/dominion) -- Epoch-based encrypted content access control
